title: Colosseum (Flavian Amphitheatre)
summary: The Colosseum, or Flavian Amphitheatre, in the centre of Rome, is the largest amphitheatre in the world. Begun under Vespasian in 70 CE and finished under his son Titus in 80, it staged gladiator fights and animal hunts for about 50,000 spectators. Games were banned in 438 CE, and in the Middle Ages the ruin was quarried for stone.

uncertainty.note: Start is the year construction began, 70 AD (Roma Capitale tourism office); Texas Tech's record has it 'begun ad 75' and gives 75-96 as the creation dates. Completion in 80 AD under Titus. End is the present: the ruin stands.

phases.description: Commissioned by Vespasian on the site of Nero's artificial lake; construction began in 70 AD and ended in 80 AD under Titus (Texas Tech has it begun in 75).
Gladiator fights (munera), animal hunts (venationes) and naumachiae staged for about 50,000 spectators; a fire damaged the whole monument (its date is not given in the source).

After Valentinian III abolished the games in 438 the building 'underwent a progressive decline'; in the Middle Ages and Renaissance it was a quarry, an animal shelter and a place of workshops and homes.

reviewer_note: Shape arena. Least sure of the start year (70 AD per Roma Capitale, 75 per Texas Tech) and the arena size (76 x 46 m vs 86 x 54 m; the wooden floor is lost, so both are reconstructions). Height 48 m is the lower figure; Texas Tech gives 48.5 m. Material span for the cavea and wooden floor is limited to the period of use (80-438) because later survival is not sourced. Coordinates are the POINT printed on the Turismo Roma page, matching UNESCO's Italian component point.
